Artificial

/ar-tih-FISH-uhl/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Artificial means made by human skill or effort rather than occurring naturally; not genuine or spontaneous

The hospital lobby's cheerful plants turned out to be entirely artificial, requiring no water or sunlight at all.

Worked Example

When the town's only lake dried up during the drought, city officials trucked in thousands of gallons of water to fill a newly built artificial pond nearby, hoping to keep the local wildlife from leaving the area entirely.

The pond didn't form naturally through rainfall or a spring — humans built and filled it deliberately, which is exactly the distinction "artificial" makes.

How Artificial Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

synthetic

synthetic: stresses that something was chemically manufactured rather than grown or found

man-made

man-made: a plain, direct phrase for anything humans built or produced

fabricated

fabricated: emphasizes deliberate construction, sometimes with a hint of dishonesty

Antonyms

natural

natural: occurring in nature, without human creation

genuine

genuine: real and authentic, not manufactured or faked

How Strong Is It? — man-made → artificial → synthetic

man-made vs. artificial

man-made vs. artificial: Something man-made is simply built or produced by people, which could include anything from a chair to a dam.

synthetic vs. artificial

synthetic vs. artificial: Something synthetic is specifically manufactured through a chemical process, often to imitate a natural substance.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of artificial.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — art-

Root — art-: skill, craft (Latin ars/art-)

Root — fic-

Root — fic-: to make (Latin facere)

Suffix — -ial

Suffix — -ial: relating to

Put it together

Put it together: "Artificial" literally means "relating to something made by skill" — combining art- ("skill, craft") with fic- ("to make"), it describes anything produced through human craft rather than occurring on its own.

Use the root in a new word: artifact

Use the root in a new word: artifact: Archaeologists carefully cataloged every artifact recovered from the ancient burial site.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Artificial is a neutral, descriptive word — it simply distinguishes human-made from naturally occurring, without necessarily implying anything is fake or deceptive (compare 'imitation,' which more strongly suggests deception).
